Treatment summary
Patient presented following a low-speed collision in a parking lot, reporting neck and
low back strain. The mechanism of injury is consistent with the reported symptoms, and
the initial presentation was reasonable for a soft tissue strain of this kind. There is
no known prior injury to the cervical or lumbar regions. Over the course of care, the
patient completed 44 visits, with additional services added progressively over several
months. The duration and scope of treatment have extended well beyond what is
typically required for a strain of this severity. Imaging of the cervical and lumbar
spine was within normal limits. Observed movement outside the examination room was
unrestricted and did not match the range of motion described during formal testing.
Billing records reviewed for this episode show no duplicate or repeated charges for
the same service.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.
